items.feedback: Right: the loop of choose an action, run it, feed the result back is what makes a system an agent. A longer prompt or a bigger model only changes what a single call can do, not the structure around it.

You picked 'the calendar entries, read by opening the booking system on its own'. The model only writes text: at this point its output is a request naming check_calendar with the laser cutter and tomorrow's date as arguments (option c). The program around the model runs the tool and sends the calendar entries back. It is tempting to think the model does the action, because from the outside the assistant seems to look things up itself.

Right: when the agent repeats the same failing step, more steps and more context add nothing. A step limit that stops the loop and reports back is a safeguard the program provides, and the makerspace assistant needs one too, since every extra step costs money.

The answer is 4, not 1. Each model call ends with one tool request or the final answer, so the three tool requests take three calls and the final answer takes a fourth. The program runs the three tools between those calls; the model never runs them itself inside one call. A quick check: count the inputs the model receives, which are the question and three tool results, so four.

'It sends it back to the model' is the right first half. What is missing is why: the model needs the result as part of its next input so it can decide its next step or write the final answer. Without that, the loop could not continue. Next time, add the purpose in a short 'so that...' clause.

Your first sentence is right: the model is sent a list of tools, each with a name and a description, and picks the one that fits the request. The second sentence is wrong. The model does not remember its past choices on its own; each session starts empty unless the program saves something and puts it back into the model's input. Memory between sessions is something we design, and it is the next topic.

summary: You have the core of the agent loop: you spotted what defines an agent, you know a step limit is needed, and you know the model chooses tools from their descriptions. The idea to fix is who does what. The model only writes text, either a tool request or a final answer, and the program runs the tools (q2, q4). You also assumed the model remembers earlier sessions by itself (q6); it does not. Next step: redraw your laser cutter trace with two columns, 'model' and 'program', and mark who does each step. Then bring the question 'what does the model see in each call?' to the context and memory lesson.
